They range from small and simple, like a blood glucose meter, to large and complicated, like a ventilator. You might use one at home or at work, or you may need one in a hospital. To use medical devices safely: Know how your device works. Keep instructions close by Understand and properly respond to device alarms Have a back-up plan and supplies in the event of an emergency Keep emergency numbers available and update them as needed Educate your family and caregivers about your device Food and Drug Administration Start Here Medical Device Safety (Food and Drug Administration) Related Issues Medical Device Safety Communications (Food and Drug Administration) MedWatch, the FDA Safety Information and Adverse Event Reporting Program (Food and Drug Administration) Specifics Full-Body CT Scans: What You Need to Know (Food and Drug Administration) Home Healthcare Medical Devices: A Checklist (Food and Drug Administration) Needles and Other Sharps (Safe Disposal Outside of Health Care Settings) (Food and Drug Administration) Clinical Trials ClinicalTrials.gov: Equipment and Supplies (National Institutes of Health) Journal Articles References and abstracts from MEDLINE/PubMed (National Library of Medicine) Article: A machine learning framework to adjust for learning effects in medical...
